{"skill":"Poetry","work":{"kind":"poem","text":"The rain comes down on the tin roof,
a steady drumming through the night.
I lie awake and count the drops
until the window turns to light.
In the morning puddles hold the sky,
and the street smells clean and new.","title":"Rain on the Roof"}}

{"skill":"Poetry","work":{"kind":"poem","text":"Steam lifts from the pepper buns
like a promise no one keeps for long.
The fortune teller folds her table
while the squid man sings the same three notes
he sang to my mother.
I buy what I always buy.
The lanterns hum their red vowels
and for a moment the whole street
is a sentence I can almost translate.","title":"Night Market, Raohe Street"}}
{"skill":"Recipe writing","work":{"kind":"recipe","text":"Cook rice with tomato and pepper. Add stuff and stir. Its very nice when its done.","title":"Jollof rice"}}

{"skill":"Recipe writing","work":{"kind":"recipe","text":"Serves 2.

Ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, sliced; 1 red pepper, sliced; 1 onion, sliced; 2 tbsp soy sauce; 1 tbsp oil; 1 tsp grated ginger.

1. Heat the oil in a wok over high heat.
2. Fry the chicken for 5 minutes until cooked through.
3. Add the pepper, onion and ginger and fry for 3 minutes.
4. Add the soy sauce, stir and serve with rice.","title":"Chicken stir-fry"}}

{"skill":"Recipe writing","work":{"kind":"recipe","text":"Makes a big jar (about 900 g).

500 g plain flour, 120 g caster sugar, ½ tsp grated nutmeg, ½ tsp fine salt, 100 g cold butter in cubes, 1 large egg, 150 ml cold milk, sunflower oil for frying (about 1 litre).

1. Whisk the flour, sugar, nutmeg and salt. Rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like fine breadcrumbs, about 3 minutes. Don't let it warm up: warm butter is what makes chin chin chewy rather than crisp.
2. Beat the egg into the milk, pour it in and bring it together into a firm dough. Knead for only a minute, just until smooth.
3. Roll it out 5 mm thick (no thicker, or the middles stay soft) and cut 1 cm squares.
4. Heat the oil to 170°C. Fry in small batches, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're the colour of a digestive biscuit, not just golden.
5. Drain on paper and leave them to cool completely before tasting: they crisp as they cool. Stored airtight, they keep three weeks.","title":"Crisp chin chin"}}
